title: Does the job with style and ease
body:
Great little app. It’s easy to see days or months or weeks or years, even hours and minutes and down to the second if you want to know that!  So you can count by whatever metric you want. 

You can have multiple counters going at once to keep track of different things which I haven’t needed to do but is a really neat functionality. 

It keeps track of how many times you’ve reset the counter if you want to keep that of that, what your longest streak was, you can set goals and reminders (you could set a milestone and have your phone beep at you to remind you to celebrate when you get there!) and look at stats for each individual thing you’re keeping track of. 

it manages to do all that but still be very very easy to use as a basic timer if you aren’t interested in any of that functionality.  looks good while being no frills, which you’d doesn’t think matters too much for a basic counter, but for something like this it really does make a difference for the experience of opening the app and seeing the number to be a pleasant, frictionless one.  

I wouldn’t change anything about it. Thanks devs

title: Days Since App
body:
I have been using this app for a little over 145 days and it has helped motivate me to quit a few difficult habits that I have held onto for the past few years. This app makes goals more tangible and allows you to track the frequency of your habits. The success of not engaging in certain habits and viewing this on the ‘Days Since’ app also increases motivation which often overrides the rush of dopamine you get when you are engaging in those difficult-to-break habits. Although I do recommend this app, there are some improvements that I think would make this app 100x better: 
1) Creating little badges/stickers which could be awarded for completing short-term goals of going a certain number of days without engaging in a habit. Ideally, this would pop up when you first open the app and (if notifications are enabled) possibly as a notification on the users home screen. 
2) Although there is some benefit in the small counting “bubbles” that keep track of various different habits in one place, they are somewhat less noticeable when they are viewed altogether. I find that when I look at them in this format, I don’t feel as accomplished. I’m not entirely sure if there is a better alternative. Perhaps it would be better if the goal counting numbers were bigger? Perhaps it would be better if there were relevant images attached to make them more engaging/stand out more? 
3) I find that I feel more accomplished when I check things off a list manually. Because the app automatically counts days and nothing is checked off, if feels as a more passive way of keeping track of habits (which is not necessarily bad); however, I do feel it would be beneficial to have certain milestones (eg: 10 days, 1 month, etc…) which users could manually check off or “acknowledge” by pressing some sort of button. This would not only separate the days into seemingly more achievable little goals which eventually equate to quitting entirely but would also make users feel like they are playing a part in the tracking process, thereby motivating them to continue.

title: A good motivator, clean design.
body:
The app does what it says it does, and the widget option is great! Very useful to see everything at a glance. 
Keeping a streak isn’t the perfect motivator for breaking a bad habit, but it is a useful tool. I really like the option to leave a note when you reset the timer. It makes you consider what led to the break in streak. 

Perhaps the addition of some notifications when you reach milestones (like 1 week, 2 weeks, 1 month, 50 days, 100 days, etc) will help you celebrate the goal and also keep the fight in mind. 
Maybe an option to note your reasons why you want to break the habit. These motivators are usually the ones that count.

title: Great and Simple
body:
Days since is an easy to use and user friendly app, there are no ads or micro transactions or subscription trash you’ve got to pay for, just straight up simple counters. 

The counters show hours, days, weeks, months and years, has reset features and a stat log with how many resets you have, days since you’ve started, longest streak and average streak, 

Additionally, the app includes a calendar with timelines, privacy features such as Face ID, Password, App Icon Customisation, You can also share the counters on social medias with sizes including Square, Portrait and Story,

Overall Days Since is an amazing app, but features that could be included are home screen widgets, a nicer counting display that isn’t just numbers occurring on a screen, such as “I am Sobers” bar graph counter and lastly notifications for new milestones for days, weeks, months, and years.

title: Great Counting App
body:
I used to use another very similar app but it hasn’t received updates in two years. That app still looks good & functions well, but it doesn’t have new things like widgets. 

Days Since is an elegant way to track anything (smoking/drinking/days since an accident at your nuclear power plant etc.) It has different colours for each counter, the ability to change between hours, days, months etc.

title: Better than “I Am Sober”!
body: It has been really helpful. It is really easy to use, I like it better than the very well known “I Am Sober” app. I Am Sober only lets you set up two sober streaks and you can’t customise what you’re sober from very easily because there is a limited amount of characters for their custom categories. Days Since, however, let’s you do more than two sober streaks at once, and it is very easy to use, and you can pick the colour of your category which is fun. I really like it. 5/5 stars.
